headline: Growth holds, margins widen, buybacks power EPS higher
summary_short: Revenue was $1,400.1M, up 7.6% y/y (3.7% organic constant-currency) though down 0.5% q/q; GAAP operating margin expanded to 8.3% from 7.6% y/y while diluted EPS rose 18.8% y/y to $1.52, aided by a 5.4% smaller diluted share count from ongoing buybacks.
summary_long: Revenue rose 7.6% y/y to $1,400.1M (3.7% organic constant-currency, aided by a ~3.9pp FX tailwind) but fell 0.5% q/q. GAAP operating margin improved to 8.3% from 7.6% y/y (non-GAAP 14.3% vs 13.5%); diluted EPS was $1.52, +18.8% y/y, helped by a 5.4% smaller diluted share count after $324M of Q1 buybacks, including a $300M accelerated repurchase. Operating cash flow swung to -$36.4M from +$24.2M y/y, not explained in the release. Cash fell to $1,037.0M from $1,296.1M q/q, mainly the buyback spend. For FY2026, EPAM now guides revenue growth to 4.0%-6.5%, GAAP diluted EPS to $8.29-$8.59; full-year GAAP/non-GAAP operating-margin ranges (10%-11% / 15%-16%) were held unchanged.

drivers.explanation: CEO Balazs Fejes called Q1 a strong start to the year, citing steady execution and continued momentum on the company's AI-native and AI-foundational transformation initiatives.
Reported revenue growth of 7.6% y/y included a favorable FX effect of roughly 3.9 points; stripping that out, organic constant-currency growth was 3.7%, with no inorganic contribution.

GAAP operating margin rose to 8.3% from 7.6% y/y (non-GAAP 14.3% vs 13.5%); cost of revenue grew only 6.3% y/y against 7.6% revenue growth, expanding gross margin and flowing through to operating income.

Diluted EPS growth of 18.8% y/y outpaced net income's 12.3% rise because diluted shares outstanding fell 5.4% y/y, consistent with the quarter's $324M of buybacks including a $300M accelerated repurchase.
Cash fell about $259M q/q mainly because the company spent $324 million on share repurchases in the quarter, including $300 million for the previously announced accelerated share repurchase.
